chosen.premise: When hungry, Hypno puts humans to sleep, tastes their dreams, and carries away anyone having a good one.
chosen.hook: Hypno doesn’t just make you dream—it chooses the best dreams to steal.
chosen.visualIdea: Clues appear in sequence: hunger, a sleeping person, dream bubbles, then a glowing good dream carried away.
chosen.note: Distinctly Hypno: it targets sleepers, samples dreams, and carries away people having good dreams. The escalating sequence creates an unusually strong mystery and visual payoff.

candidates.premise: Hypno’s pendulum can put even someone who just woke up to sleep in three seconds.
candidates.hook: Hypno can put you back to sleep in just three seconds.
candidates.visualIdea: A three-second countdown plays as Hypno’s pendulum swings, then the scene instantly fades into sleep.
candidates.note: A precise, highly visual claim directly stated in the Diamond entry; slightly less unique because other hypnosis-based Pokémon could support a similar sleep hook.

candidates.premise: Hypno’s hypnosis lasts longer when it swings its pendulum for longer.
candidates.hook: With Hypno, every extra swing makes the sleep last longer.
candidates.visualIdea: A pendulum timer stretches from a short swing into a long arc while a hypnosis effect bar keeps growing.
candidates.note: A Hypno-specific rule with strong textual support, though the effect is harder to depict convincingly than the three-second claim.

candidates.premise: The same Hypno described as extremely dangerous is also called a savior by people needing sleep.
candidates.hook: Hypno is both a dangerous predator and someone’s sleep specialist.
candidates.visualIdea: Split-screen Hypno: one side shows danger warnings, the other shows a hospital patient peacefully falling asleep.
candidates.note: The danger-versus-medical-helper contrast is well supported and visually clear, but it is a broader profile angle rather than one sharply quantified fact.

candidates.premise: In Alola, Hypno’s main target is Komala, yet it rarely harms people.
candidates.hook: Hypno has a main target—and in Alola, it usually isn’t humans.
candidates.visualIdea: A target board shifts from human silhouettes to Komala while a caption highlights “rarely harms people.”
candidates.note: The Komala detail is surprising and visually distinctive, but the cited entries do not fully establish why Komala is the main target or reconcile that claim with Hypno’s broader dream-predator behavior.

candidates.premise: Drowzee becomes Hypno by leveling up at exactly level 26, gaining a pendulum-wielding second stage.
candidates.hook: At level 26, Drowzee turns into the Pokémon with the pendulum.
candidates.visualIdea: A level counter reaches 26 as Drowzee flashes into Hypno, with the pendulum appearing in its hand.
candidates.note: The level-26 transformation is concrete and easy to animate, but evolution-at-a-level is a common Pokémon angle and the evolution method is supported by secondary rather than official data.
